summary:
I've written the scorecard and run it on both of today's hulls. It takes 19 s on baseline_fine.stl (843,846 triangles) and 9 s on 01_skrog.stl, including all renders. Today's hull fails three V10 requirements: deck outline max deviation 13.4 mm (limit 12.5), strake height max deviation 15 mm, and minimum hull-side wall 0.05 mm. It also scores poorly on smoothness: 17 % of adjacent-triangle angles on the hull skin are above 5 deg in 01_skrog.stl.

What the scorecard does:
- **Frame:** detects the plate frame by itself and fits the angle (45.00 for 01_skrog.stl). A test copy turned to 46 deg with the bow reversed gave identical numbers.
- **x position:** anchored on the mast hole (centre = 3400). If no mast hole is found, the bow tip is put at x = 4.
- **Draft:** an STL with the keel at z = 0 cannot show draft directly, so it is checked through the rudder-pin holes, which are built at z = -90/-200.
- **Measured lines:** frozen copies of the measured tables are built into the script, so later edits to params.py do not move the target.
- **Deck edge:** taken as the virtual intersection of side and deck, so a rounded V10 edge is judged on the same line as today's sharp one. On today's hull this matches the actual corner within about 1 mm.
- **Holes:** found by slicing the mesh. Today's positions are saved in the script as the reference for later rounds.
- **Wall thickness:** rays cast inward from about 30,000 sampled points on the hull side and deck.
- **Renders:** 6 flat-shaded views lit like Bambu Studio, plus 4 photo-matched views. Rendering runs in parallel threads.
- **Photo cameras:** solved once from traced hull outlines (20-22 px fit error on the iPhone photos, focal length fixed at 1490 px) and from 6 landmarks for IMG_9370 (8 px). Treat these as a visual check, not a measurement.

Things to know before using the numbers:
- **Strake height** is measured as the centre of the strake band seen from the side. The strake is tilted to follow the hull, so its visible band sits 7-15 mm below its centreline on the hull. Measured at the outer face of the strake instead, the error grows to 21 mm.
- **Fairness counts depend on the triangle mesh.** Even baseline_fine.stl has topside triangles 100-250 mm long. Use them to compare rounds, not as absolute numbers. I added a "ripple" measure because the fine-scale sign-change count gave the coarse mesh a better score than the fine one, which is misleading.
- **The trace aft of the keel (x 6470-7440) is a dead-flat line**, probably not the hull bottom. The script reports it but marks it uncertain.
- **The 4 shells are closed and manifold.** tools/meshcheck.py still reports 124 (fine) / 4 (skrog) non-manifold edges. Those come from vertices less than 0.1 µm apart that its 1e-4 mm weld merges, and they are harmless. Note that meshcheck exits 1 on 01_skrog.stl because of this.

Findings in today's hull:
1. **Stanchion holes run out through the topside.** The x=3550 holes (7 mm deep in the model) break out through the flared side just above the strake: about a 45 mm slot full scale, 1.5 mm in the model. At x=1450 and 2500 the remaining wall is under 0.5 mm.
2. **Deck holes open into the hollow.** They open six of the void compartments to the outside, and 10 of the 20 holes are surrounded by solid material for only 50 mm of their 210 mm depth.
3. **The keel's leading edge is far from the drawing.** The model has a straight edge; the traced drawing has a much fuller keel, up to about 400 mm apart around x=4000.
4. **The forefoot is too shallow.** The canoe body is up to about 40 mm above the trace around x=1650.
5. **The bow head-on photo shows a different forefoot shape.** The real boat has a sharp V below the waterline; the model has a round U.

During the camera fitting I ran out of memory twice on this shared 16 GB machine, and other agents were building hulls on it at the same time. I stopped only my own fitting processes and reran them with fewer workers. The scorecard itself uses threads and stays well within memory.

Files are in C:/Users/stig/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/12681ed4fad82730/bbd7b4f2-5285-465a-8464-b20ca4b41c67/scratchpad/v10/score:
- score.py
- out/baseline_fine_score.json and out/baseline_fine_score.png
- out/skrog_today_score.json and out/skrog_today_score.png
- dev/fit_onland.py, dev/fitmulti.py, dev/fit9370.py (the camera fits)

Nothing in the repo or the worktrees was changed.
usage:
python score.py HULL.stl [--frame auto|plate|boat] [--out DIR] [--name TAG] [--ref REF.json] [--anchor auto|mast|bow] [--xbow 4.0] [--rays 30000] [--photos DIR] [--no-render] [--jobs 6]

HULL.stl can be the plate-placed 01_skrog.stl (turned on the bed; the angle is fitted, normally 45 deg) or a boat-frame STL from build_hull_only.py. The frame is detected automatically.

Outputs:
- DIR/TAG_score.json: all numbers; lengths are full-scale mm unless the key ends in _model. "summary" holds PASS/FAIL against the V10 requirements and the change against the reference.
- DIR/TAG_score.png: 1600 px wide sheet with the score table, 6 flat-shaded views, 4 photo pairs (photo with the model outline in cyan, next to the model rendered with the same camera), and plots of line deviations, underwater profile, curvature, sections and wall thickness.

Defaults:
- DIR defaults to <script folder>/out.
- REF defaults to out/baseline_fine_score.json, so every V10 round is compared with today's hull automatically.
- --no-render gives numbers only, in about 10 s.

Examples:
  cd C:/Users/stig/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/12681ed4fad82730/bbd7b4f2-5285-465a-8464-b20ca4b41c67/scratchpad/v10/score
  python score.py ../baseline_fine.stl --name baseline_fine
  python score.py C:/Users/stig/Documents/GitHub/HR26-modell/export/stl/01_skrog.stl --name skrog_today
  python score.py <v10_round.stl> --name v10_rN
